types.embedding_query_text: SportsTeam: A group of athletes who play together in a sport, often representing a specific city or organization. Also called athletic club, squad, franchise, side. Examples: Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Dodgers, The Los Angeles Lakers, the basketball team.

chosen_type.label: SportsTeam
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org SportsTeam class perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and examples, explicitly including 'Los Angeles Lakers' as an example.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, man, woman. Examples: Bob Iger, Josh Kushner, Donald Trump, Jared Kushner.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person class directly corresponds to the OIE_TYPE definition of an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A quantity of money, typically expressed with a currency and amount. Also called currency amount, financial value, price, cost. Examples: $12.5 billion, $10 billion.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MonetaryAmount class accurately represents a quantity of money with currency, matching the OIE_TYPE and examples like '$12.5 billion'.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: Industry: A category of economic activity characterized by a particular type of goods or services. Also called sector, business field, market. Examples: US Sports Industry, US sports.

chosen_type.label: IndustrySector
chosen_type.definition: A broad classification of businesses based on the primary economic activity they engage in.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents the abstract concept of an 'Industry' as a category of economic activity; existing candidates are organizations or locations.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation

candidates.label: LocalBusiness

Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: SportsClub

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: A company or institution responsible for gathering, producing, and disseminating news and information. Also called media outlet, news agency, broadcaster, publisher. Examples: CNN, ESPN, The Wall Street Journal, the Journal.

chosen_type.justification: The schema.org NewsMediaOrganization class is a direct and precise match for the OIE_TYPE, explicitly defining organizations that produce and disseminate news.

candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization

Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time, typically a day, month, and year. Also called calendar day, specific day, point in time. Examples: August 12, 2026, Last October, Wednesday, 12/08/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Date data type is the exact match for representing a specific calendar date, as described by the OIE_TYPE and examples.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement. Also called metropolis, town, urban area. Examples: Los Angeles.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org City class is a direct and precise match for the OIE_TYPE definition and the example 'Los Angeles'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.embedding_query_text: GoverningBody: An official group or organization that controls or manages an activity or organization. Also called regulatory authority, board, council, administration. Examples: NBA Board of Governors, the NBA’s Board of Governors.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization

candidates.label: SportsTeam

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: TVSeason

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific number or amount of something. Also called amount, number, count, total. Examples: 17 championships.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Number data type is the most appropriate for representing a count of discrete items like '17 championships', rather than a continuous measurable quantity.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: SportsSeason: A defined period within a year during which a particular sport is actively played or competed. Also called athletic season, competition period, playing season. Examples: 2019-20 NBA Season, 2019-20 season.

Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.comment: A PodcastSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason representing a single season of a podcast, used when a podcast is structured into distinct seasons. Also called podcast series season. Examples: "Serial" Season 1, "Lore" Season 3, a specific season of a narrative podcast. Distinct from PodcastSeries, which is the entire podcast collection.

candidates.label: SportsEvent

types.embedding_query_text: InvestmentFirm: A company that manages financial assets and makes investments on behalf of clients or itself. Also called asset management company, financial institution, fund manager. Examples: Guggenheim Investments, Walter’s Guggenheim Investments, Guggenheim’s.

chosen_type.label: FinancialService
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org FinancialService class explicitly lists 'investment firm' as an example, making it a perfect match for 'InvestmentFirm'.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: InvestmentFund
candidates.comment: An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. Also called mutual fund, hedge fund, pooled investment vehicle. Examples: Vanguard S&P 500 Index Fund, a private equity fund, a real estate investment trust (REIT). Distinct from InvestmentOrDeposit, which is a broader category for financial products requiring fund transfers for potential returns.

candidates.label: BrokerageAccount
candidates.comment: A BrokerageAccount is an InvestmentOrDeposit financial product that allows an investor to deposit funds and place investment orders through a licensed broker. Also called investment account, trading account, stock account. Examples: Fidelity brokerage account, Charles Schwab investment account, E*TRADE account. Distinct from BankAccount, which is for general deposits and withdrawals.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

types.embedding_query_text: Occupation: A job or profession. Also called profession, job, vocation, career. Examples: Sports Deals Banker, one banker involved in sports deals.

candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

types.embedding_query_text: Complaint: A formal statement expressing dissatisfaction or grievance. Also called grievance, protest, accusation, charge. Examples: Internal Whistleblower Complaint, an internal whistleblower complaint.

chosen_type.label: Statement
chosen_type.justification: A complaint is a type of declaration or assertion, making the schema.org Statement class a suitable general fit.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

types.embedding_query_text: Investigation: A formal inquiry or systematic examination to discover and examine the facts of a matter. Also called inquiry, probe, examination, scrutiny. Examples: Federal Investigation, a federal investigation.

chosen_type.label: CheckAction
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org CheckAction class explicitly includes 'investigating' in its definition, making it a strong match for 'Investigation'.

candidates.label: CheckAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

types.embedding_query_text: Company: A commercial business enterprise. Also called firm, corporation, business, enterprise. Examples: Guggenheim Parent Company, Disney, Guggenheim’s parent company.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Corporation class explicitly lists 'company' as an alias and fits the definition of a commercial business enterprise.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.embedding_query_text: HoldingCompany: A company that owns controlling shares in other companies but does not produce goods or services itself. Also called parent company, umbrella company, investment company. Examples: Thrive Eternal.

chosen_type.label: HoldingCompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that owns controlling shares in other companies but does not produce goods or services itself.
chosen_type.justification: While a holding company is a Corporation, no schema.org candidate provides a more specific type for this distinct business structure.

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: VacationRental
candidates.comment: A lodging business that offers single properties for rent for limited periods, typically for vacations. Also called holiday rental, short-term rental, vacation home. Examples: an Airbnb apartment, a beach house rental, a cabin in the mountains.

candidates.label: SelfStorage
candidates.comment: A local business providing rental units for individuals and businesses to store their belongings. Also called storage facility, mini-storage, public storage. Examples: 'U-Haul Self-Storage', 'Extra Space Storage', 'Local Storage Units'.

candidates.label: LodgingBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business that provides temporary accommodation for travelers or guests. Also called accommodation provider, hospitality business, hotelier. Examples: a hotel, a motel, an inn, a bed and breakfast, a resort. Distinct from Hotel, which is a specific type of lodging business.

types.embedding_query_text: InvestmentSector: A specific area or industry targeted for financial investment. Also called investment area, market segment, asset class. Examples: Sports and Entertainment Investments, sports and entertainment investments.

chosen_type.label: InvestmentSector
chosen_type.definition: A specific area or industry targeted for financial investment.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents an 'InvestmentSector' as a category for financial investment; existing candidates are financial products or services.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: InvestmentFund
candidates.comment: An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. Also called mutual fund, hedge fund, pooled investment vehicle. Examples: Vanguard S&P 500 Index Fund, a private equity fund, a real estate investment trust (REIT). Distinct from InvestmentOrDeposit, which is a broader category for financial products requiring fund transfers for potential returns.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: AutomatedTeller
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by a machine for banking transactions. Also called ATM, cash machine, automated banking machine. Examples: "Bank of America ATM", "Wells Fargo cash machine", "independent ATM kiosk".

types.embedding_query_text: Informant: A person who provides information, often confidentially, to an organization or individual. Also called source, tipster, whistleblower, confidant. Examples: Person Familiar with the Matter, a person familiar with the matter, the person familiar with the matter, the source.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: An 'Informant' or 'Person Familiar with the Matter' describes a function or capacity a person holds, which aligns well with the schema.org Role class.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.embedding_query_text: Spokesperson: A person who is chosen to speak officially for a group or organization. Also called representative, mouthpiece, delegate, agent. Examples: Guggenheim Spokesperson, a spokesperson for Guggenheim’s parent company.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: A 'Spokesperson' describes a function or capacity a person holds within an organization, which aligns well with the schema.org Role class.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: SpeakableSpecification
candidates.comment: A specification indicating, typically via CSS selectors or XPath, which sections of a document are particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called speakable content definition, text-to-speech markup, voice-friendly section. Examples: a specification highlighting the main article text on a news page, a definition for a recipe's ingredients list.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: TouristInformationCenter
candidates.comment: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.
